correctness.rationale: A complete elementary proof establishes invariant 0<x<=1, strict monotonicity of the prey-only map and y extinction for all beta<=theta(1+alpha). At equality a positive y limit forces x to 1 but then forces exponentially negative prey drift, contradiction. The liminf/limsup map argument and invariant lower barrier give the 0/s/1 trichotomy. For recovering orbits, an affine contraction bounds u/v, proving u/v->1/(a(1+alpha)); reciprocal predator increments then tend to theta/[a(1+alpha)^2] and Cesaro proves both claimed 1/n amplitudes. Explicit substitution proves above-threshold coexistence. 36 exact-rational identities, 6 equilibria, and 3 forward trajectory diagnostics passed; experiments alone are not proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A fixed-point multiplier with modulus at most one is not a proof of global exclusion in a nonlinear two-population map, especially at unity. The explicit new steps are global monotone predator decay, asymptotically autonomous monotone prey classification, a bounded u_n/v_n ratio, and the precise reciprocal-increment constant. These are not straightforward corollaries of the cited local results.

value.rationale: The paper provides numerical Allee-induced extinction thresholds and local multipliers. This theorem distinguishes all-orbit predator exclusion from mere local stability at the neutral boundary and quantifies an open recovering regime. The leading prey deficit is universally (1+alpha)/theta independent of both Allee parameters, a mathematically meaningful prediction for a natural parameter cut rather than a numerical local normalization test. The exact y coefficient records the Allee dependence and helps discriminate prey versus predator recovery.
